Unplugged Performance Debuts Tesla Model Y L Suspension Packages
8 photos
Photo: Unplugged Performance
Unplugged Performance is giving Tesla Model Y L customers more ways to customize their long-wheelbase sport utility vehicles. Suspension upgrades reign supreme on this occasion, with the California-based specialist introducing no fewer than four distinct packages for the family-oriented version of the Model Y.
These suspension upgrades are joined by expanded compatibility with the company's existing wheel and brake offerings. The OEM+ Flush Fitment Kit and Perfect Flush Fitment Kit are both focused on stance and wheel positioning. The Big Three combines anti-roll hardware with lowering springs, while Core Four and Street & Trail add some well-deserved lift.
Starting with the OEM+ Flush Fitment Kit and Perfect Flush Fitment Kit, these packages use 15-millimeter (0.6 inches) wheel spacers and adjustable rear camber arms. The spacers push the wheels outward, bringing them closer to the fender edges for a meaner look, whereas the camber stuff helps the Model Y L in terms of alignment while also lowering the vehicle.
Care to guess which is the biggest difference between said packages? Springs is the right answer, indeed, with Unplugged Performance advertising mild lowering springs and moderate lowering springs, respectively. The Big Three suspension package brings together either mild or moderate lowering springs, adjustable rear camber arms, and sway bars for both ends.
Considering the aforementioned list, the Big Three also changes the cornering behavior of the Model Y L. As you're well aware, sway bars are designed to resist body roll when cornering, thus controlling how much the body leans during rapid changes of direction and through bends. Both spring options come with the very same front and rear sway bars.
Photo: Unplugged Performance The Core Four package, meanwhile, trades lowering springs for a suspension lift. Its components are sway bar end links, adjustable rear camber arms, a Luxury-spec rear sway bar, and the Leveling Lift Kit. According to Unplugged Performance, this combo should be perfect for occasional use on rural roads.
Additional clearance should also help when negotiating steep driveways. Lastly, what Unplugged Performance calls Street & Trail combines touring-oriented suspension goodies with a leveling kit.
Adjustable shocks are on the menu as well, and the off-road rear sway bar is a self-explanatory upgrade over the standard Model Y L. At $4,395 as of this writing, this package is the most expensive and comprehensive of the four.
UP has further validated three spring height options for the zero-emission sport utility vehicle. The Stock Height Dual Rate Springs retain the factory ride height. Alternatives include mild and moderate lowering springs. For maximum versatility, the stock height is recommended. Wheel choices round out this announcement, with UP offering square configurations exclusively.
For staggered fans, the UP-03 and UP-05 are forged wheels that measure 19 inches by 9.5 and 10 inches, respectively, with an ET30 offset. This arrangement allows Model Y L customers to transfer the original factory rubber directly to the Unplugged Performance wheels. A set of four wheels will set you back anything from $3,235 to $5,595 if ordered directly from Unplugged Performance.
